subject: POC: schedule sync — throughput scope, demo agenda, and load plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@oakbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC: schedule sync — throughput scope, demo agenda, and load plan

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, we'd like to get a short POC kickoff + hands-on session on the calendar that covers three specific items:

- Prompt review & acceptance criteria (golden prompts for quality checks)
- Routing / model variant walkthrough (latency vs cost tradeoffs)
- Load testing/benchmarking window (throughput targets, SLOs, and test harness)

Proposed dates/times (PT):
- Tue Dec 14, 10:00–11:30
- Wed Dec 15, 14:00–15:30
- Thu Dec 16, 09:00–10:30

If none work, please suggest two slots and we’ll adapt. For the load testing piece, could you share target TPS and p99 latency SLOs so we size the harness appropriately? A quick example from other engagements: target 350 req/s peak, p99 < 400ms on the short prompt path.

I’m attaching a short runbook draft (redwood-runbook-v1.pdf) — it contains the proposed test steps and the minimal telemetry we’ll need from your side (API credentials, traffic shaping rules).

Next steps (if you confirm a slot):
1) We’ll send calendar invites and include the runbook + load-targets spreadsheet.
2) Karthik will lead the routing/config section.
3) Soojin will coordinate the test harness and validation scripts.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-runbook-v1.pdf (12 KB)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@oakbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@oakbank.com
Date: Fri, 03 Dec 2027 12:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC: schedule sync — throughput scope, demo agenda, and load plan

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear plan. All three agenda items look good. Quick notes from our side:

- Our initial target for the POC is 250 req/s sustained with 500 req/s short bursts. We want p95 < 250ms and p99 < 600ms for the primary routing path.
- We will need to run some of the load windows outside business hours (US banking core schedules) — evenings after 7pm PT or early mornings before 6am PT are safest.
- I’ll need a short SOC 2 artifact (summary) for procurement, but that can come later this week.

Available slots: Dec 15 14:00–15:30 PT works for our engineers (DevOps can join). If you prefer evening testing windows, we can do Dec 16 19:30–21:30 PT for the load run.

Please send a calendar invite with the confirmed slot and the attendee list.

Thanks,
Elena
Platform Lead — OakBank
elena.ruiz@oakbank.com | +1 617-555-2244
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@oakbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC: schedule sync — throughput scope, demo agenda, and load plan

Thanks Elena — Dec 15 14:00–15:30 PT is locked for the kickoff/dry-run. We’ll plan the load window for Dec 16 19:30–21:30 PT (evening slot) as you recommended. I’ve attached an editable spreadsheet (oakbank-load-targets.xlsx) that captures the targets you mentioned — please confirm the columns marked "required from OakBank" (API host, test token, allowed IPs).

Action items for this thread:
- Elena: confirm the spreadsheet fields and add any additional telemetry requirements.
- Karthik: validate routing variants and prepare a short slide (5–7 min) about fallback behavior.
- Soojin: prepare harness repo link + smoke tests; will coordinate required compute footprint.
- Marissa: I’m looping you in on this one to help run the customer-facing portion and to capture post-run notes.

Forwarding two quick notes below that we’ll use in the kick-off:

---
Marcus Lin (on runbook):
We’ll do an initial prompt acceptance check (10–15 prompts), then increase RPS in 3 steps (10%, 50%, 100% of target) holding each for 3 minutes while we monitor p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost. If latency exceeds SLOs, we’ll step back and exercise the lower-cost variant.
---

I’ll send the calendar invite in the next hour and include the runbook + targets spreadsheet.

Cheers,
Marcus

Attachments: oakbank-load-targets.xlsx (8 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@oakbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC: schedule sync — throughput scope, demo agenda, and load plan

Marcus / team —

Couple of technical clarifications before the run:

1) Routing variants: we’ll prepare three configurations for the demo — low-latency (float16 on A100s), cost-optimized (int8 quantized on T4-like), and fallback safe-mode (smaller model with KV cache disabled). I’ll bring performance numbers for each.

2) Test harness: Soojin, can you confirm whether the harness will replay golden prompts with interleaved synthetic traffic? We should include a short-burst traffic generator to validate burst smoothing.

3) Telemetry: we’ll ingest p50/p95/p99, token counts, GPU utilization, and request size distribution. If OakBank can provide a sandbox token and an allowlist for our ingress IPs we’ll be able to run the full harness without hitting production controls.

Note: For the evening load window (Dec 16 19:30–21:30 PT), we estimate needing two x A100 equivalents for the 500 req/s short-burst validation. If OakBank wants to run with smaller compute, we can scale down and adjust expectations. I’ll include this data point in the kickoff slide.

— Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: (referenced) performance-variant-matrix.xlsx (will circulate before kickoff)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@oakbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC: schedule sync — throughput scope, demo agenda, and load plan

Sounds good — thanks for the quick turnaround.

We’ve confirmed the following:
- Kickoff/dry-run: Dec 15, 14:00–15:30 PT (Elena + DevOps + backend product).
- Load test window: Dec 16, 19:30–21:30 PT (DevOps will be on-call).
- Targets confirmed in spreadsheet: 250 sustained / 500 short-burst; p95 < 250ms, p99 < 600ms.

I’ve uploaded the sandbox token to the spreadsheet and added the allowed IP range under the "required from OakBank" column. SOC 2 summary attached to a separate procurement thread — procurement says that’s fine to accept post-signature.

Please send calendar invites and include the calendar ICS for the load window so our DevOps pager can pick it up. Also, include a short pre-kickoff checklist in the invite body (smoke test passed, runbook attached, contact list).

Looking forward to it.

Best,
Elena
